correctness.rationale: The two-sided three-round game on a vertex-transitive graph reduces to the set of adjacency-and-extension spectra over distinct ordered pairs; a missing third pattern can be played on either side. For cyclic separation d, a 00 witness exists exactly when the longer gap n-d exceeds 2r+1. For nonedges, 11 exists exactly when d≤2r, and the only pair missing both one-sided witnesses is the antipodal nonedge at n=2r+2: regularity equates one-sided counts, and a common-neighbor count over the two arcs attains 2r only there. Adjacent pairs have distinct closed neighborhoods and a common neighbor precisely for r≥2. Re-evaluating the ranges d≤r and r<d≤floor(n/2) gives the displayed ten distinct rows; the six genuine-power rows all occur at r=2. At n=4r+2 two antipodes dominate, while at n≥4r+3 at most 4r other vertices can be covered, proving strict fixed-radius sharpness including r=1.
residual_risks: The frozen scripts were inspected, not executed. Their recorded tail and representative comparisons are finite corroboration; the all-parameter conclusion follows from the arc and game arguments.
